headline: Large User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill requires data centers and other large energy users consuming 25 MW or more to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity, preventing these costs from being passed on to residential customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Dominion Energy, Senator L. Louise Lucas, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling.
opponents: Data center industry, Data Center Coalition.
news_headline: Virginia governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers. Critics say her tweaks weaken them.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393 and SB 253, which aim to shift energy costs to data centers and large manufacturers, potentially saving residential customers money. Critics argue the governor's amendments, particularly regarding the data center tax exemption, weaken the original intent of making data centers pay their fair share.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities providing water to data centers to report monthly water consumption data to the State Water Control Board, increasing transparency on data center water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental advocacy groups, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, communities concerned about water resources.
opponents: Data center industry (potential opposition to increased reporting burden).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, mandates that local water authorities report data center water usage, making the numbers publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide greater transparency regarding the industry's water consumption, a growing concern for communities.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities (HEUF) like data centers, requiring site assessments for sound profiles near homes and schools, and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community advocates, environmental groups, Del. Joshua Thomas.
opponents: Data center industry (due to potential restrictions and increased development costs).
news_headline: Virginia passed 15 data center bills in 2026, including siting restrictions.
news_summary: Virginia passed several data center bills in 2026, including HB 153, which introduces new permit processes for large facilities, mandating sound assessments near residential areas and schools. Localities can now also require impact assessments on water, agriculture, and historic sites before approving data center projects.
